symptom: On a Mendix 11.14.0 project written only by mxcli, `mxcli fix property-sets` reported seven MIXED names and filled none: `MIXED  ODataPublish$EntitySet.ReadMode: on 42 of 60 element(s); without it: … [ODataPublish$PublishedODataService2 F1AdminApi]`, `MIXED  ODataPublish$PublishedMicroflow.Parameters: on 2 of 5 element(s); only on: …`, and on one domain model `DomainModels$DateTimeAttributeType.LocalizeDate` (15 of 16) plus `DomainModels$NoGeneralization.HasOwnerAttr` / HasChangedByAttr / HasChangedDateAttr / HasCreatedDateAttr (81 of 84). mx check was clean (ako/mxcli#1805)
cause: Two different causes behind one report. (1) A current writer branch: publishedEntitySetToGen wrote each of the four modes only `if es.XMode != ""`, and publishedMicroflowToGen wrote Parameters only `if len(pm.Parameters) > 0`; the doctype gate never took those branches (10-odata states all four modes on every set and its one action has parameters). (2) Stored state: no writer of today omits the domain-model keys (entityToGen writes all four flags and LocalizeDate since #743/#1373), but an older mxcli wrote only the true flags and no LocalizeDate, and every later domain-model write rebuilds only the entity it names and passes the siblings through as stored bytes. The table had no row for any of the ten keys, because it is measured from what today's writers leave out, so neither the next write nor the repair could fill them
file: `mdl/backend/modelsdk/odata_write.go` (publishedEntitySetToGen writes all four modes; publishedMicroflowToGen always writes Parameters, RegisterMandatoryPropertyList for the empty [3]); `modelsdk/canon/studiopro_property_defaults.json` (10 rows, since 10.24.24); tests `mdl/backend/modelsdk/issue1805_odata_property_sets_test.go`, `modelsdk/canon/propertyset_issue1805_test.go`, `modelsdk/mpr/property_set_issue1805_test.go`, `cmd/mxcli/cmd_fix_property_sets_issue1805_test.go`; bug-test `mdl-examples/bug-tests/1805-property-sets-mixed-odata-and-domain-model.mdl`
insight: **Tell a writer bug from stored state by running every write path on a fresh app before reading any code**: one MDL script through create, create or modify, add/modify attribute, association, alter of a sibling, rename and move, plus the OData service with stated and unstated clauses, then `fix property-sets --dry-run`. What reproduces (the OData names, on 10.24.24, 11.13.0 and 11.15.0) is a writer; what does not (the domain-model names) is an element an older build stored, and only a measured table row reaches it — on the next write of its unit (completion at the choke point) or by the repair. **A writer that branches on an optional clause is invisible to the doctype gate** unless a script leaves the clause out: grep the writer for `if x != ""` / `if len(x) > 0` around a part, not only for the key name. **Strip-and-convert measures a row no writer leaves out** (#1505's method): strip the key from every element of the type, `fix hashes --repair`, `mx convert -p -s` a copy, and what convert writes back is the row; ReadSource, ChangeNotSupported, [3], false and true were identical on all three versions, and testdata/testapp-views' 11.14.0 Studio Pro entity set carries the same four modes. **Once a table row exists, completion hides the writer bug from every storage-level test at or above its floor**: the census test through the backend passed with the writer fix reverted; only the encoded-document test (codec.Encoder on the converter, no storage) failed. Keep both: the writer fix is what covers 10.4–10.24.23, below the floor. Side effect worth knowing: describe now prints all four modes for a set created without them (as it always did for a Studio Pro-authored one), and that output re-checks clean
